scope: Diagnostic replay of already generated source-local bodies. It may use up to three model calls and one source-verified authored comparison. This is separate from the one-call primary comparison.

OPERATIVE.record:
On 30 October 2023 the Council adopted United Kingdom draft S/2023/808 by 15 votes to none as resolution 2704 (2023). [VOTE]

[OPERATIVE] The Security Council extended the mandate of the UN Verification Mission in Colombia until 31 October 2024, as detailed in Resolution 2704, operative paragraphs 1 and 2. This extension was granted based on the expressed willingness of the Council to collaborate with Colombia's Government on a further extension of the mandate, contingent upon an agreement between the parties.

[OPERATIVE] The official authority paragraph confirms the actor as the Security Council, which adopted the act of extending the existing UN Verification Mission to the specified date. The separate future position recorded indicates the Council's readiness to pursue additional extensions only if mutually agreed upon by the Colombian Government and the relevant parties.

[OPERATIVE] The delegation statement reiterates the Council's stance on the provisional extension, emphasizing that any subsequent mandate prolongation remains subject to the specific conditions of an inter-party agreement. This aligns with the documented speaker's representation of the Security Council's limited overlap in granting new authority without a finalized bilateral accord.

The resolution granted new EMC authority only for the interim

ADDITIONAL.record:
On 30 October 2023 the Council adopted United Kingdom draft S/2023/808 by 15 votes to none as resolution 2704 (2023). [VOTE]

Resolution 2704, final preambular paragraph. The Council expressed willingness to consider Government–EMC monitoring and verification only upon the Secretary-General's confirmation of a ceasefire with appropriate verification protocols, explicitly taking into account his update on the implementation of Resolution 2694.

Resolution 2694 had already extended the Mission's role to monitoring and verification of the Government–ELN ceasefire, establishing the existing authority for that specific conflict.

The Government–EMC legal stage remains distinct, with no verification granted here; the separate input requires the Secretary-General's confirmation and update on Resolution 2694 before any consideration.

The limited overlap exists solely regarding the Secretary-General's confirmation and update on Resolution 2694, but the resolution did not grant new EMC authority, as verification for the Government–EMC was not approved.

BRAZIL.record:
On 30 October 2023 the Council adopted United Kingdom draft S/2023/808 by 15 votes to none as resolution 2704 (2023). [VOTE]

[S/PV.9461, p. 3] The presiding representative, speaking in national capacity for Brazil, stated that the Council must respond to the priorities expressed by Colombia's Government, affirming that the resolution reflects Colombia's sovereign will. Brazil explicitly supported the Government's total peace strategy.

[S/PV.9461, p. 3] Brazil urged the Council to authorize verification of the Government–EMC ceasefire only when the situation is sufficiently mature, emphasizing the need for conditions to be fully met before such verification proceeds.

[S/PV.9461, p. 3] The limited overlap between Brazil's call for mature conditions and the resolution's authorization indicates that the resolution granted new EMC authority contingent upon the maturity of the ceasefire verification process.

A3.record:
On 30 October 2023 the Council adopted United Kingdom draft S/2023/808 by 15 votes to none as resolution 2704 (2023). [VOTE]

Ghana, speaking for the three African Council members, welcomed the unanimous mandate extension and supported Mission monitoring and verification in the EMC case contingent on the Secretary-General's conditions [A3].

The delegation emphasized a separate priority to encourage progress on the Ethnic Chapter for Afro-Colombian and Indigenous people [A3].

With the official authority paragraph and both delegation statements present, the resolution granted new EMC authority while noting the limited overlap between the ceasefire confirmation requirement and the distinct Ethnic Chapter priority [A3].
